statement: Let S=[[0,1,1,1],[-1,0,1,-1],[-1,-1,0,1],[-1,1,-1,0]], and let rho(a,b,c) have correlated block A=a I_4+i b S on span{|ii>} and diagonal entry c on each |ij>, i!=j, with a,b,c real. The operator is PPT iff a>=sqrt(3)|b| and c>=|b|, and EVERY nonzero PPT member has Schmidt number at most 2, with the explicit rank-two orbit construction below. On the PPT boundary c=|b| and b!=0 it is separable iff a>=3|b|; for sqrt(3)|b|<=a<3|b| it is PPT entangled of Schmidt number exactly 2. This is one continuously parameterized, intrinsically frustrated phase-covariant family, not an unrestricted 4x4 PPT/SN3 resolution.
PPT: S^T=-S and S^2=-3I, so iS is Hermitian with eigenvalues +/-sqrt(3), each twice. The correlated block A is PSD iff a>=sqrt(3)|b|, and the twelve offdiagonal diagonal entries require c>=0. The partial transpose consists of four singleton a blocks and six blocks [[c,i*b*S_ij],[-i*b*S_ij,c]], so is PSD iff a>=0 and c>=|b|. Combining the two gives the stated PPT region.
finite_local_symmetry: There are 12 signed permutations (pi,s) modulo an irrelevant global sign satisfying S_(pi(i),pi(j))=s_i*s_j*S_ij. Generators are pi=(0,2,3,1), s=(1,1,1,1), and pi=(1,0,3,2), s=(1,-1,-1,1); their permutation group is A4, transitive on the 12 ordered pairs. The local unitary pair is (P_pi diag(s)) tensor P_pi. It preserves rho. First twirl a ket under U tensor conjugate(U), U diagonal; then average over these 12 local unitaries. For any coefficient matrix X with diagonal z, the resulting correlated block is a'I+i*b'*S with a'=||z||^2/4 and b'=z^*(iS)z/12, while all offdiagonal populations are c'=sum_(i!=j)|X_ij|^2/12. To see the correlated form, ordered-pair transitivity and preservation of S force each offdiagonal to be a common scalar times S_ij; Hermiticity makes that scalar purely imaginary. The formula for b' follows from (iS)^2=3I and trace((iS)^2)=12. The continuous diagonal-phase twirl can be replaced by the 4^3 choices U=diag(1,i^p,i^q,i^r), since all character exponents lie in [-2,2]; with the 12 group elements it gives a finite 768-ket rank-preserving twirl.
separable_region: For |b|<=a/3, form for every pair i<j a two-coordinate vector u_ij with |u_i|=|u_j|=sqrt(|b|) and u_i*conjugate(u_j)=i*b*S_ij. It is the diagonal-amplitude vector of a product ket with both offdiagonal populations |b|; a diagonal-phase twirl gives correlated [u_ij] and those populations. Summing the six pair twirls gives A=3|b| I+i*b*S and all p_ij=|b|. Add (a-3|b|) sum_i[|ii>] and (c-|b|) sum_(i!=j)[|ij>], both nonnegative, to obtain an explicit separable decomposition.
rank_two_region: For a>0 and a/3<=|b|<=a/sqrt(3), set C=iS and choose unit eigenvectors u_+,u_- of C with eigenvalues +/-sqrt(3), for example u_+/-=(e_0 +/- C e_0/sqrt(3))/sqrt(2). Let p=(1+sqrt(3)*|b|/a)/2 and z=2*sqrt(a)*(sqrt(p)*u_sign(b)+sqrt(1-p)*u_-sign(b)). Then ||z||^2=4a and z^*C z=12b. For b!=0 all four displayed coordinates of z are nonzero. Put U=|z_0*z_1|+|z_2*z_3|>0. By 2|xy|<=|x|^2+|y|^2, 2U<=4a<=12|b|. Choose t>0 satisfying t^2+t^(-2)=12|b|/U. Define X as a direct sum on pairs (0,1) and (2,3), with diagonal X_ii=z_i, X_ij=t*sqrt(|z_i*z_j|), X_ji=z_i*z_j/(t*sqrt(|z_i*z_j|)), and all other entries zero. Each 2x2 block has determinant zero, so rank(X)<=2, and its offdiagonal squared norm is 12|b|. The finite local twirl of [X] therefore equals rho(a,b,|b|). Adding (c-|b|) sum_(i!=j)[|ij>] gives an explicit Schmidt-rank<=2 decomposition for every PPT member in this region. The boundary cases b=0 or a=0 are already separable.
entangled_boundary: On c=|b|>0, every 2x2 PPT block is rank one, so |A_ij|^2=p_ij*p_ji for all pairs. In any hypothetical separable decomposition, phase-twirl every product atom. The pairwise Cauchy-Schwarz equality then forces each atom's diagonal-amplitude vector z to have pair phases agreeing with A wherever both entries are nonzero. Every triangle product A_ij*A_jk*A_ki is non-real, so no such z can have three nonzero entries. Hence each contributes at most two indices and satisfies sum_i|z_i|^2>=2*sum_(i<j)|z_i*z_j|. Summing and using the triangle inequality yields trace(A)>=2*sum_(i<j)|A_ij|=12|b|, so a>=3|b|. Thus a<3|b| proves entanglement, while the previous construction proves separability at and above that boundary.
explicit_example: rho(1,1/2,1/2)/10 has trace one, birank (16,10), is PPT entangled and has Schmidt number 2. One exact rank-two seed has diagonal z=(1,1,-i,-1) and two rank-one blocks: X_01=phi, X_10=phi^(-1), X_23=phi, X_32=i*phi^(-1), phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. It has ||z||^2=4, z^*(iS)z=6 and offdiagonal squared norm 6; its 768 local-unitary orbit projectors average to the unnormalized rho. This example is independent of the separately stopped historical JL audit and is not a Schmidt-number-three witness.

The first checker's seed-determinant output was only a comment-level assertion; the second checker supplies the actual Q(sqrt5) calculation. limits: This is an exact explicit decomposition for the stated three-parameter family and an entanglement classification only at c=|b|. It does not classify entanglement when c>|b|, other phase-covariant states, or the unrestricted 4x4 problem. No novelty, external or formal review claim.
